definitions.explanation: A small movable stall or cart set up outdoors to sell food and drinks, commonly seen at festivals and in entertainment districts.
A large decorated float or portable stage pulled through streets during festivals.

examples.japanese: {屋台|やたい}でラーメンを{食|た}べた。
examples.english: I ate ramen at a food stall.

examples.japanese: {祭|まつ}りの{屋台|やたい}で{焼|や}きそばを{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought yakisoba at a festival stall.

examples.japanese: {福岡|ふくおか}の{中洲|なかす}には{屋台|やたい}がたくさん{並|なら}んでいて、{観光客|かんこうきゃく}に{人気|にんき}がある。
examples.english: Nakasu in Fukuoka is lined with food stalls and popular with tourists.

examples.japanese: {豪華|ごうか}な{屋台|やたい}が{通|とお}りを{進|すす}む。
examples.english: An ornate festival float parades down the street.

examples.japanese: {秋|あき}{祭|まつ}りでは{地区|ちく}ごとに{屋台|やたい}を{出|だ}す。
examples.english: Each district brings out its own festival float for the autumn festival.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちは{屋台|やたい}の{上|うえ}で{太鼓|たいこ}を{叩|たた}きながら{町|まち}を{練|ね}り{歩|ある}いた。
examples.english: The children paraded through town beating drums atop the festival float.

notes:
KANJI:
{屋|や} (roof/shop) + {台|たい} (stand/platform).

SENSE 1 — FOOD STALLS:
{屋台|やたい} food stalls are a major part of Japanese street food culture. Fukuoka's {中洲|なかす} district is especially famous for its {屋台|やたい} serving ramen, {焼|や}き{鳥|とり}, and {おでん|おでん}. Festival {屋台|やたい} sell items like {焼|や}きそば, {たこ焼|や}き, {綿菓子|わたがし}, and {りんご飴|あめ}.

SENSE 2 — FESTIVAL FLOATS:
In festivals like the {高山|たかやま}{祭|まつ}り and {秩父|ちちぶ}{夜祭|よまつり}, {屋台|やたい} refers to large ornate floats pulled through the streets.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {屋台|やたい}を{出|だ}す: to set up a stall / bring out a float
- {屋台|やたい}で{食|た}べる: to eat at a stall
- {屋台|やたい}{村|むら}: a cluster of food stalls
